newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia pre-election violence claims two lives.
newsitem.headline: Colombia pre-election violence claims two lives.

text.p: Gunmen dragged two municipal officials out of their homes in southwestern Colombia on Friday and shot them dead in a new bout of pre-election violence, local authorities said.
The head of the municipal council in the town of Caldono and a local government appointee were shot execution-style outside their homes before dawn and the gunmen fled, they said.
Local radio quoted police and Caldono Mayor Dodamin Trujillo as saying they had no clues as to who was responsible.
In a telephone interview with Reuters on Thursday, Trujillo predicted that the run-up to October's elections was likely to lead to bloodletting.
"These may not be very healthy elections," he said, saying he and other municipal officials had received a growing number of death threats in recent weeks.
Leftist rebels and right-wing death squads have vowed to prevent candidates they oppose from standing in the October elections.

Also on Friday, the mayor of Caicedo in the northwestern province of Antioquia was kidnapped by suspected rebels, the fourth mayor abducted in the province this month. The other three mayors have been released.

The state insurance agency La Previsora has offered a campaign season insurance policy that will pay the medical and funeral expenses of candidates injured or killed in the run-up to the October vote. At least 20 mayors have been killed in the last 18 months.
